newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ITC finds evidence of carbon steel dumping. [CORRECTED 20:34 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S. ITC finds evidence of carbon steel dumping. [CORRECTED 20:34 GMT]

text.p: The U.S. International Trade Commission (ITC) said Wednesday it found "reasonable indication" that U.S. industry was injured by imported carbon steel plate from China, Russia, South Africa and Ukraine.

As a result of the preliminary determination, the Commerce Department will continue to conduct anti-dumping investigations and will make its preliminary findings known around April 14, 1997, the ITC said in a statement.
The investigations could eventually lead to anti-dumping (corrects from countervailing) duties.

"The ITC found that there is a reasonable indication that a U.S. industry is materially injured or threatened with material injury by reason of imports of cut-to-length carbon steel plate from China, Russia, South Africa and Ukraine," the ITC said.
The ITC, a federal body that probes trade complaints, was investigating a petition filed by Geneva Steel Co and Gulf States Steel Inc.
